candidates.reading: English Standard Version, Leviticus 16:29–31; Hebrew critical-text comparison outstanding
candidates.shared: Both prescribe religious self-denial/fasting in a communal framework.
candidates.difference: Leviticus specifies the tenth day of the seventh month, cessation of work, and atonement; Q2:183 prescribes fasting and emphasizes God-consciousness, with Ramadan identified at 2:185.
candidates.limits: The Hebrew idiom 'afflict yourselves' needs philological review; do not imply the Qur'an reproduces the Day of Atonement fast.

candidates.reading: English Standard Version of Isaiah 58:3–7; Hebrew comparison outstanding
candidates.shared: Both concern fasting in relation to proper religious conduct.
candidates.difference: Isaiah rebukes oppressive and quarrelsome fasting and commands justice and aid for the poor; Q2:183 announces a fasting obligation and its purpose.
candidates.limits: No shared event or demonstrable textual dependence; broad ethical comparison may be more suitable for Cross-References.

candidates.reading: English Standard Version of Deuteronomy 20:10–18; Hebrew comparison outstanding
candidates.shared: Both texts regulate conduct in armed conflict.
candidates.difference: Deuteronomy distinguishes distant cities and conquest towns, allows enslavement/plunder and commands destruction of specified populations; Q2:190 addresses fighting those who fight you and forbids exceeding limits. Their legal situations and normative scopes differ.
candidates.limits: Do not equate the texts' war rules or infer borrowing; interpret 2:190 with surrounding verses and diverse early tafsir.
